newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran seizes drugs, arrests smugglers in southeast.
newsitem.headline: Iran seizes drugs, arrests smugglers in southeast.

text.p: Iranian police seized 234 kg (516 lb) of drugs in the southeastern province of Kerman in the past week and arrested 17 smugglers, the official news agency IRNA reported on Monday.
"Of the total, 113 kg (249 lb) were seized from the armed smuggglers and the remaining 121 kg (267 lb) discovered in inspection of vehicles passing through the province," it said.

Iran, a key route for drugs being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan, said last week it had erected barbed wire fences, dug trenches, and set up hundreds of checkpoints and watchtowers along its borders to prevent traffickers from entering the Islamic republic.
It said that in the year to March 1997, 175 tonnes (385,800 lb) of various narcotics had been discovered by the Iranian authorities and 16,000 drug dealers arrested.

According to Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 lb) of opium or 30 grams (just over one ounce) of heroin is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
